newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end easier on stock rally.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end easier on stock rally.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures ended easier on Monday after a rally by Tokyo stocks.
But the downside was underpinned by short-covering when the December neared support at 98.81, traders said.
"Sentiment has worsened since last Friday when an LDP (Liberal Democratic Party) official said Japan could raise interest rates by early autumn," said a city bank dealer.
Koji Omi, deputy chairman of the LDP's Policy Research Council, said on Friday that he saw a chance of a credit tightening in Japan by early autumn, given improving economic fundamentals.

Bearishness persisted on Monday as the Nikkei stock average sprinted to a strong close. The Nikkei rose 383.04 points, or 1.91 percent, to finish at 20,451.85, propelled by futures and blue-chip buying interest.
The key December Euroyen futures ended 0.03 lower at 98.82 after moving between 98.81 and 98.86. Turnover was 55,962 contracts.
Japanese banks continued to pay fixed interest rates in the short-term Interest Rate Swap (IRS) market, another factor keeping the topside for Euroyen futures capped, traders said.
"It seems that the market may request a rate hike by trying the downside before the BOJ releases its key tankan corporate survey (on June 25)," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank.

The key contract briefly fell as low as 98.75 last Thursday, the lowest intraday level for any benchmark contract since July 24, 1996, ahead of industrial output data on the mistaken belief that the figures might be strong.
In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate was traded at around 0.51 percent, up from Friday's 0.50 percent.
Banks' need to raise funds for tax payments on June 4 was providing upward momentum, traders said.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) maintained a slightly accommodative credit stance for a third day on Monday.
The BOJ left the market with a surplus of around 100 billion yen after its morning operation.
Long-end benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CD) were not issued but were offered at 0.59 percent, down from Friday's 0.60 percent. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
